contradicting_evidence: Current breadth is heavily negative, and all observed alt-capitalization proxies underperform BTC; persistent weakness could produce a directional downside outcome.
Negative settled ETH ETF flows and modest seven-day stablecoin contraction weigh against assuming a durable recovery.

frozen_forecast.expected_path: There is insufficient evidence to prefer a higher or lower broad-market endpoint over one week. Selective recovery attempts and renewed weakness both remain credible. This is uncertainty about net direction, not a forecast of low volatility or sideways trading.
falsification_conditions: A persistent BTC/ETH recovery, stronger ETH/BTC, broader participation and improving settled flows would establish an upside case.
Repeated price deterioration accompanied by persistently weak breadth, falling ETH/BTC and continued negative settled flows would establish a downside case.
A single rebound, flow session or proxy-breadth improvement would not by itself resolve the weekly uncertainty.
missing_evidence: No sustained sequence covering the relevant weekly horizon establishes persistence in prices, participation or capital flows.
Updated settled ETF sessions, liquidity deployment evidence and a current dominance trajectory are needed to assess whether demand broadens.
Unavailable microcap coverage prevents inference about full-market transmission.
supporting_evidence: Current short-window altcoin weakness contrasts with positive 90-day median alt returns and modest median outperformance versus BTC; neither alone determines the coming week.
Stablecoin supply signals are mixed: modest seven-day contraction but modest 30-day expansion, without confirmed deployment.
The latest settled ETF session is split between a small BTC inflow and a larger ETH outflow, rather than demonstrating uniform demand.
BTC/ETH price stabilization and slight ETH/BTC improvement coexist with worsening breadth, leaving competing recovery and retest paths.
